statusNote: Applications are currently not open to the India / Asia-Pacific region.
summary: The MLH Fellowship is a fully remote, 12-week internship alternative run by Major League Hacking. Fellows work in small groups (pods) on real open source and partner projects with guidance from expert mentors.

stipend.headline: Educational stipend
stipend.detail: Depending on the program track, fellows receive either an educational stipend or university credit. MLH does not publish the amount; it depends on the length and content of the program and is stated in the educational agreement you sign when accepted. U.S. residents may receive a tax document from the payment provider.
notes: The fellowship is funded by employers, so places depend on employer demand.

facts.label: Time commitment
facts.value: About 20 hours per week (about 15 on the project)

facts.label: Region
facts.value: Not open to India / Asia-Pacific applicants at present

eligibility: Living in a country not embargoed by the United States; the Production Engineering track requires living in the U.S., Canada or Mexico.
Able to commit at least 20 hours per week.
Know how to code in at least one programming language and speak English proficiently.
Have taken part in at least one MLH hackathon or Global Hack Week event.
Have a video-call-quality internet connection (30 Mbps minimum recommended).
Currently not available to applicants in India and all Asia-Pacific countries, because no employer funding the fellowship is hiring in the region.
howToApply: Apply on fellowship.mlh.io with essays and a code sample (clean, original, documented work).
Qualified applicants go through interviews and a final review.
Candidates are matched to projects by language, framework, timezone and availability; rejected applicants can reapply for a later batch.
